newsitem.title: SWEDEN: No-confidence vote vs Sweden's Persson defeated.
newsitem.headline: No-confidence vote vs Sweden's Persson defeated.

text.p: A no-confidence vote against Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson was defeated in the Swedish parliament on Friday.

Voting was 204 against, 119 in favour of the no-confidence motion. There were 16 abstentions. Three opposition parties tabled the motion against Persson following criticism of his remarks allegedly praising political stability in China.
Ten deputies in the single-chamber parliament were absent.
Persson, prime minister since March, was supported by his ruling Social Democrats, and by the Leftist and Centre parties.
The Conservatives, Liberals and Christian Democrats voted for the no-confidence motion. The Green party abstained.

Persson, speaking before the vote, dismissed the no-confidence motion as "an early election campaign" and said his remarks in Beijing had not been intended to convey any political approval of Chinese policy.
